about: The people's Blender-built assets (D-307; the D-305 pipeline, tools/blender/build.mjs). Per asset: the node source (the project's own bodies and pieces; nothing shaped by hand), the Blender script, the node post-step, the files it writes to public/models/people/, the inputs whose hash decides staleness, budgets and the ledger row. tests/people_models.test.ts holds them to it; src/people/peopleModels.ts loads them.

people_hair.title: strand cards for scalp hair, the bob, the bunch at the nape, long and short beards and brows, and their strand atlas

args.args_note: C throughout, after the reliefs (hair to the nape bunched behind, the long beard to the upper chest cut square: outfits.ts LEN 0.12 m below the chin) and MATERIAL_CULTURE 'Hair and beards'. Spacing (m) between card roots on the surface; len, width, lift [root, tip] (m); the second layer of scalp hair shorter and lifted (volume, a broken outline). Atlas: 2048 px, 8 columns x 4 rows (cells 256 x 512 px: ~80 um a pixel across a 2 cm card, so a strand is about one pixel wide); rows straight/wavy, natural curls, ringlets (the rolled curls of the court dressing), fine (brows, short hairs); curl radius and pitch as shares of the cell (natural curl ~4 mm across, ringlets ~3 mm: C). classRows: card class (0 scalp and nape, 1 beards, 2 brows) -> atlas row per hair style (0 natural, 1 court, 2 straight). The MakeHuman CC0 hair textures give each strand its shade (their luminance along the strand).

source.args_note: C throughout, after the reliefs (hair to the nape bunched behind, the long beard to the upper chest cut square: outfits.ts LEN 0.12 m below the chin) and MATERIAL_CULTURE 'Hair and beards'. Spacing (m) between card roots on the surface; len, width, lift [root, tip] (m); the second layer of scalp hair shorter and lifted (volume, a broken outline). Atlas: 2048 px, 8 columns x 4 rows (cells 256 x 512 px: ~80 um a pixel across a 2 cm card, so a strand is about one pixel wide); rows straight/wavy, natural curls, ringlets (the rolled curls of the court dressing), fine (brows, short hairs); curl radius and pitch as shares of the cell (natural curl ~4 mm across, ringlets ~3 mm: C). classRows: card class (0 scalp and nape, 1 beards, 2 brows) -> atlas row per hair style (0 natural, 1 court, 2 straight). The MakeHuman CC0 hair textures give each strand its shade (their luminance along the strand). Beards in the court dressing take the natural curls row (classRows [1,1,0]): the ringlets read as strings in the first render.

people_hair.budget_note: download <= 6 MB of T-K7's 60 MB; GPU: the atlas UASTC 2048^2 with mips ~5.6 MB (T-K8 3.5 GB); triangles per set at the full-detail LOD (the costumes' 42,000 of tests/humans_runtime.test.ts hold the sum)

people_cloth.title: garments re-cut from simulated patterns (D-322): Blender's cloth solver settles every garment piece's cut, refined to a 1.5-2.6 cm mesh, on a reference body of each group (men, women, children), outer layers over the settled garments under them; every level of detail samples the settled cloth, low-passed to what it can carry

source.args_note: C throughout. The cut's ease (wide cut / fitted) after the dress research: the women's many-folded dress (IR-WOMEN, B for 'many-folded') 1.3; the knee-length tunics 1.15; the court robe 1.06 (its pleats are the reliefs' and pressed into the cut's rest shape: drape.ts ROBE; more ease would undo them). D-322: the upper garments are cut 4 % fuller than their fitted shells between the pins (over the shoulders, under the belt: they blouse and fold instead of hugging the torso), the trousers 8-10 % about each leg below the waist band. Cloth: Blender's cloth settings for a medium wool or linen (vertex mass 0.2 kg, tension 15, shear 5, bending 0.5, the robe's stiffer 1.0, the dress's softer 0.3), quality 7, collision 4 mm off the body, 72 frames at 24 fps (3 s: the drape settles), the gathered waist drawn in over the first 20. Resolution (D-322): each piece's full-detail cut is Loop-subdivided until its mean edge is at most `edge` (2.6 cm): the simulations run at 1.3-2.6 cm; every level of detail samples the settled cloth at its own vertices through a Gaussian of `lowpass` × its edge length (what the level can carry without aliasing). Groups' reference bodies: m03 (the outfits' reference), f02, c01. Arms are not colliders for skirts, upper garments and trousers (they swing in the game). Gathers: the waist of a gathered skirt is drawn in along a wave of 10 folds whose length is the wide cut's, so the cloth below buckles into folds; the court robe is not gathered (its pleats are pressed). The belt cinches: under it the upper garment is drawn in to 6 mm off the torso, the skirt's top band to 12 mm. D-313: the belt is a tied sash (outfits.ts sashGeo): its band and knot pinned (from 3.5 cm below the belt's centre up), the two hanging ends free below, softer (bending 0.15). D-322 stage 2 (`over`): the sash settles over the group's settled skirt (men the tunic skirt, women the dress), the headcloth over the settled dress (D-313's see-through: it had settled on the body alone, inside the dress), the veil over the settled robe, the kandys over the settled tunic; each is kept `gap` (4 mm) outside them as drawn at each level. One drape set per group serves every costume of the group (the court robe takes the tunic's sash).

people_cloth.budget_note: download <= 3 MB (T-K7); no triangles or maps: the drape moves the pieces' own vertices (the costumes keep their budgets)
people_cloth.ledger: People's garment drape from Blender's cloth solver (public/models/people/people_cloth.*; D-307)
